newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's ProSieben posts 18 pct Q1 ad sale growth.
newsitem.headline: Germany's ProSieben posts 18 pct Q1 ad sale growth.

text.p: German private television channel Pro Sieben said on Tuesday it had boosted its gross advertising income in the first quarter of 1997 by 18 percent, placing it second for growth among private German stations.

Pro Sieben took 641 million marks in gross advertising income between January and March of this year, its marketing company MediaGruppe Muenchen (MGM) said, based on data provided by Nielsen S&P Werbeforschung, a market research company.
Nielsen S&P compiles advertising figures, which it provides to media clients.
Kabel 1, owned by Bavarian media group Kirch Gruppe, posted gross advert income of 105 million marks in the first quarter of 1997, a 42 percent leap from the previous quarter.
MGM said RTL remained the top station in advertising sales with 848 million marks in gross ad income during the three-month period, a seven percent climb.
Berlin-based channel Sat1 reported a 13 percent drop in gross ad income during the first quarter of the year with gross advertising income of 606 million marks.
Gross advertising income is calculated from the list prices of a station's commercials. Net income substracts volume discounts and agency commission from this figure.
